subtitle: How a Gond Queen Turned Monsoon Fury into a Kingdom of Water

panels.shot: wide aerial over monsoon-soaked Jabalpur basin, tanks gleaming like scattered mirrors, with Madan Mahal fort on a rocky hill
panels.action: Rani Durgavati & Diwan Adhar Kayastha stand on the ramparts of Madan Mahal, looking over a landscape of full stone-banked tanks and green fields stretching to the Satpura hills under storm clouds.

dialogue.text: In the age of Rani Durgavati, near Jabalpur, the Gonds forged a kingdom not only of forts and spears, but of water itself — a power remembered today in tanks like Ranital, Cherital and Adhartal.

i18n.hi: रानी दुर्गावती के समय, जबलपुर के पास, गोंडों ने सिर्फ़ किलों और भालों का नहीं, पानी का भी राज्य गढ़ा — जिसे आज रानीताल, चेरीताल, अधारताल जैसे ताल याद दिलाते हैं।

panels.shot: low aerial sweeping along the Narmada valley, clouds piling over Satpura hills, river glinting below
panels.action: Monsoon clouds gather over the Satpura hills as the Narmada curves through rocky gorges, forests and scattered clearings near the future Jabalpur, with tiny hamlets tucked by streams.

dialogue.text: Central India in the sixteenth century: the Narmada cuts through stone, the Satpuras drink the monsoon, and for a few months each year, water roars, rushes and flows away.

i18n.hi: सोलहवीं सदी का मध्य भारत: नर्मदा पत्थर को चीरती है, सतपुड़ा मानसून पीते हैं, और कुछ महीनों के लिए पानी गरजता, बहता, फिर दूर निकल जाता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of parched landscape months later, cracked earth foreground, distant rocky hill with a small fort outline
panels.action: The same landscape in the dry season shows cracked fields, shrinking pools in streambeds, cattle being led to a muddy pond, and a faint silhouette of Madan Mahal hill-fort under a harsh sun.

dialogue.text: Then the clouds pass. Streams shrink to chains of pools. Fields crack. To rule here is to answer one question: how do you hold rain that wants to run away?

i18n.hi: फिर बादल सरक जाते हैं। नालों की जगह रह जाती हैं टूटी कड़ियाँ, खेतों में दरारें। यहाँ राज करना मतलब एक सवाल का जवाब देना: भागते पानी को कैसे रोको?

panels.shot: medium interior of rustic durbar at Garha, focus on Rani seated, Adhar beside her, map spread before them
panels.action: In a timber-pillared hall, Rani Durgavati sits on a simple throne, alert and intent, while Diwan Adhar Kayastha kneels beside a rough map of the Jabalpur basin drawn on cloth, streams and villages marked.

dialogue.text: Rani Durgavati, widow, regent, ruler of Garha-Katanga, listens as her diwan Adhar Kayastha traces rivers and hamlets. Their kingdom is forests, stone, shifting streams — and people who must eat.

i18n.hi: विधवा, संरक्षिका, गरहा-कटंगा की शासक रानी दुर्गावती अपने दीवान अधार कायस्थ की बातें सुनती हैं, जब वह नदियाँ और गाँव उँगली से खींचता है। उनका राज्य जंगल, पत्थर, बदलती धाराएँ — और पेट भरने वाले लोग हैं।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Adhar's hand on the map, Rani's face in background, intent
panels.action: Adhar Kayastha’s ink-darkened finger follows a line of small dots on the map representing villages near Jabalpur, as Rani Durgavati leans forward, eyes narrowed in thought.

dialogue.speaker: rani_durgavati_and_adhar_kayastha
dialogue.text: “When rain fails, the plough fails. Without grain, even brave spears grow thin.”

i18n.hi: "बारिश रूकी, तो हल रुकता है। बिना अनाज, शेर दिल भी सूख जाते हैं।"

panels.shot: wide shot on rocky hill of Madan Mahal, construction scene below, fort above
panels.action: Below the rocky height of Madan Mahal, where masons and labourers work on walls and reservoirs within the fort, Rani Durgavati and Adhar stand on a ledge, overlooking both the hill and the plain beyond.

dialogue.text: The hill-fort at Madan Mahal guards the approaches to Garha. Archaeologists later note its cisterns and channels. A fort here is not just stone in air — it is stone guiding water.

i18n.hi: मदन महल का पहाड़ी किला गरहा की राहें रोकता है। बाद के पुरातत्वविद उसकी टंकियाँ और नालियाँ गिनते हैं। यहाँ किला सिर्फ़ आसमान छूती दीवार नहीं, पानी को मोड़ती चट्टान है।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of a low-lying basin near Jabalpur with embankment under construction
panels.action: In a shallow depression outside the urban core, workers raise a broad earthen and stone embankment; carts bring earth, stone blocks are placed at the inner face, while Adhar points and Rani watches, veil drawn back.

dialogue.text: Near Jabalpur, they choose hollows where monsoon water collects. Embankments rise. Later people will call one Ranital, remembering the queen, and another Adhartal, remembering the diwan.

i18n.hi: जबलपुर के पास वे वही गड्ढे चुनते हैं जहाँ मानसून का पानी ठहरता है। बाँध उठते हैं। आगे चलकर लोग एक को रानीताल कहेंगे, रानी की याद में, दूसरे को अधारताल, दीवान के नाम पर।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on hands of workers compacting earth and placing stone facing
panels.action: Barefoot labourers tamp layers of moist earth with wooden rammers while others align dressed stone along the inner slope of the new tank, their bodies slick with rain.

dialogue.text: Gazetteers, written centuries later, will record the tradition. They do not note every hand that lifts earth, every thought behind the curve of a dam.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बाद लिखे जाने वाले गज़ेटियर इस परंपरा को दर्ज करेंगे। पर हर हाथ जो मिट्टी उठाता है, हर बाँध की मोड़ के पीछे की सोच वे नहीं लिखते।

panels.shot: wide shot of first monsoon rains filling the half-finished tank, villagers watching
panels.action: Heavy rain pours as muddy runoff rushes through a cut channel into the partially finished tank, swelling its level; villagers in simple dress stand under trees, watching the water spread behind the new bund.

dialogue.text: The first rains test the work. The tank swells, holds. Water that once tore gullies in a single season now lies still, cupped by hand-shaped earth.

i18n.hi: पहली बारिश ही काम की परीक्षा लेती है। ताल फूलता है, थामे रहता है। जो पानी पहले एक मौसम में ही नाले चीर देता था, अब हथेली-सी धरती में थम कर लेटता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rani and Adhar at tank edge, sunrise light on calm water
panels.action: At dawn, with mist rising from a full tank, Rani Durgavati stands at the stone edge, a reflection shimmering at her feet, while Adhar Kayastha gestures to fields stretching away from the water.

dialogue.speaker: rani_durgavati_and_adhar_kayastha
dialogue.text: “A fort feeds soldiers. This feeds everyone.”

i18n.hi: "किला सिपाहियों को पालता है। ये सबको खिलाता है।"

panels.shot: wide rural landscape showing tank feeding irrigation channels to fields
panels.action: From the tank’s outlet, a small stone sluice leads water into channels that snake through paddy fields; farmers guide the flow with their feet, children splash in shallows, cattle drink at the far side.

dialogue.text: Canals carry tank water into fields. In seasons when the Narmada runs low and streams hide among rocks, the stored monsoon keeps rice and millets alive around Jabalpur.

i18n.hi: ताल का पानी नालों से खेतों तक पहुँचता है। जब नर्मदा दुबली पड़ती है, नाले पत्थरों में छिप जाते हैं, तब यही जमा मानसून जबलपुर के धान-बाजरे को ज़िंदा रखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of forest edge by a tank, focus on animals and vegetation
panels.action: At the forest edge, a tank gleams amid reeds and lotus, herons stand in the shallows, fish ripple beneath, and a strip of sal forest rises behind, hinting at the wild world Mahesh Rangarajan will later describe.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars of forests and beasts will see tanks as havens for birds, fish, cattle and wild things. In Durgavati’s time, they are also instruments of rule.

i18n.hi: जंगल और जानवरों के आधुनिक विद्वान इन तालों को पक्षियों, मछलियों, मवेशियों और जंगली जीवों की शरण मानेंगे। दुर्गावती के समय में ये राज चलाने के औज़ार भी हैं।

panels.shot: medium interior of a small council at Garha, emphasis on a revenue register and Adhar speaking
panels.action: Inside a modest hall, Adhar Kayastha sits with scribes and a palm-leaf register showing villages listed by tanks and fields, while Rani Durgavati listens, hand on the hilt of her dagger, thoughtful.

dialogue.text: Tax rolls shift. Villages near water tanks carry new weight. Hydraulic works become part of Gond statecraft, linking grain, rent, soldiers and fort supplies to the slow rise and fall of stored water.

i18n.hi: माल–सूची बदलती है। तालों के पास के गाँवों का वज़न बढ़ता है। यह जल-व्यवस्था गोंड राजनीति का हिस्सा बनती है, जिसमें अनाज, लगान, सिपाही और किलों की रसद सब इस ठहरे पानी की उठान–गिरान से बँध जाते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Madan Mahal fort reservoir inside the fort complex
panels.action: Within Madan Mahal fort, a rock-cut stairway descends to a rectangular reservoir carved into the hilltop, its water dark and still under the sky, with stone channels etched into surrounding rock.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists of the Archaeological Survey of India will later list Madan Mahal as a protected monument. They note cisterns and tanks shaped for siege and drought, binding fort and water as one design.

i18n.hi: भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण के पुरातत्वविद बाद में मदन महल को संरक्षित स्मारक मानेंगे। वे घेराबंदी और सूखे के लिए गढ़ी गई टंकियाँ और ताल लिखेंगे, जहाँ किला और पानी एक ही नक़्शे में बँधे हैं।

panels.shot: split wide illustration of three different tanks: Ranital, Cherital, Adhartal, in their historical landscape
panels.action: Three panels within the frame depict different tanks near the early Jabalpur: a broad Ranital near settled houses, Cherital tucked near a smaller settlement, and Adhartal in more open land, each with embankments and fields around.

dialogue.text: Gazetteers of Jubbulpore repeat what people say: this tank is the queen’s, that the diwan’s. Cherital, Ranital, Adhartal — their exact dates blur, but memory ties them to her regency.

i18n.hi: जबलपुर के गज़ेटियर लोगों की बात दोहराते हैं: यह ताल रानी का, वह दीवान का। चेरीताल, रानीताल, अधारताल — सही तारीखें धुंधली हैं, पर यादें इन्हें उनकी रीजेंसी से जोड़े रखती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a British-era gazetteer writer in the 19th century looking over a tank, notebook in hand
panels.action: A colonial official in late nineteenth-century attire stands near a tank with a notebook and pen, observing the embankment and village life around it, while distant temples and houses frame the shore.

dialogue.text: When the British compile the Central Provinces Gazetteer, they walk these banks, note names, repeat local traditions. They do not dig embankments or date every stone, but they preserve a story of a water-wise queen.

i18n.hi: जब अंग्रेज़ सेंट्रल प्रोविन्सेज़ गज़ेटियर बनाते हैं, वे इन किनारों पर चलते हैं, नाम लिखते हैं, लोककहानी दोहराते हैं। वे बाँध नहीं खोदते, हर पत्थर नहीं गिनते, पर एक पानी-समझदार रानी की कथा बचा लेते हैं।

panels.shot: modern wide shot of the same tanks in present-day Jabalpur, buildings around, birds on water
panels.action: In a present-day view, the tanks lie within a growing city: concrete buildings ring Ranital, but the water still shines, with birds skimming the surface and people standing along steps at the edge.

dialogue.text: Today, ecologists measure fish, birds and pollution in these waters. They rarely ask who first turned these hollows into tanks, or why a Gond queen’s name still clings to their edges.

i18n.hi: आज पर्यावरणविद इन तालों के मछलियों, पक्षियों और गंदगी को मापते हैं। वे शायद ही पूछते हैं कि सबसे पहले इन गड्ढों को ताल किसने बनाया, या क्यों एक गोंड रानी का नाम अब भी इन किनारों से चिपका है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle close-up of Rani Durgavati on Madan Mahal rampart at dusk, wind in her veil, Adhar slightly behind
panels.action: At dusk atop Madan Mahal, Rani Durgavati stands against a darkening sky, veil and hair stirred by wind, looking out toward glinting patches of water in the basin below, while Adhar stands respectfully behind her.

dialogue.speaker: rani_durgavati_and_adhar_kayastha
dialogue.text: “Battles end in a day. Tanks outlive kings.”

i18n.hi: "जंग एक दिन की, ताल सौ राजाओं से लंबा।"

panels.shot: wide contemplative aerial over Jabalpur basin showing chain of tanks leading toward the Narmada at sunset
panels.action: From high above, a chain of tanks gleams like a necklace across the Jabalpur plain, leading the eye toward the distant silver ribbon of the Narmada under a fading orange sky.

dialogue.text: Rani Durgavati’s last battle will be fought with steel, but her quieter war was with drought. In the Jabalpur tanks attributed to her rule, we see a ruler measured not just by lands won, but by water held for others.

i18n.hi: रानी दुर्गावती की आख़िरी लड़ाई इस्पात से लड़ी जाएगी, पर उनकी चुप लड़ाई सूखे से थी। जबलपुर के इन तालों में, जिन्हें उनके राज से जोड़ा जाता है, हमें एक ऐसी शासक दिखती है जिसकी माप सिर्फ़ जीती ज़मीन से नहीं, दूसरों के लिए रोके गए पानी से होती है।

title_i18n.en: Durgavati's Tanks and the Water Kingdom
title_i18n.hi: दुर्गावती के ताल और जल का राज्य

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Gond Queen Turned Monsoon Fury into a Kingdom of Water
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक गोंड रानी ने बरसाती तूफ़ान को जल–राज्य में बदला
